# Dentino SMS Appointment Reminder System — v1 (build layers L1–L4)

## SOURCE OF TRUTH WARNING

All beads in this project implement features from the three Source-of-Truth documents:
- **Spec (SOT #1 — WHAT)**: `docs/spec/2026-06-28-dentino-system-spec.md` (PRIMARY)
- **TDD (SOT #2 — HOW TO VERIFY)**: `docs/tdd/2026-06-28-dentino-system-tdd.md` + bootstrap `docs/tdd/2026-06-28-dentino-bootstrap.md` (PRIMARY)
- **Strategy (SOT #3 — ORDER ONLY)**: `docs/strategy/2026-06-27-dentino-layer-strategy.md` (ORDERING ONLY — never a content source)
- **Architecture SoT (cite, don't copy)**: `docs/research/2026-06-16-dentino-appointment-messaging-research.md` v2.26.3

When implementing any bead: read the spec section + TDD test IDs the bead cites directly. The bead embeds key excerpts; the full SOT documents are authoritative. Cite research §refs/ADRs for architecture (SQL/DDL/ADR prose live there); only inline an exact SQL object if the bead literally implements it.

## Coordination Protocol (MANDATORY)

Any implementation work under this bead uses the project wrappers:
```bash
bin/br-claim <bead-id>
bin/br-complete <bead-id>   # only after committed+pushed+tests pass
```

Wrapper invocation must produce Agent-Mail `[<bead-id>] Start` and `[<bead-id>] Complete` audit messages through `bin/br-claim` / `bin/br-complete`; raw `br update --status` or `br close` is not an acceptable substitute.

## What this system is

A Supabase-backed cloud service that, on a 12:00 Europe/Kyiv daily run + automatic afternoon catch-up, reads tomorrow's remindable ClinicCards visits, sends each sendable patient a Ukrainian SMS with a personalized confirm/cancel link, captures the action through a public confirm page, and writes the allowed Confirm/Cancel status back to ClinicCards — all guarded, idempotent, reconciled, and hermetic by default. SMS-only v1 (TurboSMS primary / AlphaSMS fallback, sender `Dentino`).

## Phases (execution ORDER, not importance tiers — L4 ships in v1 like L1–L3)

1. **Data layer** (root) — `0001_core_schema.sql` + `0002_rls_policies.sql` core. Nothing else is `br ready` until this closes.
2. **L1 — Hermetic Guarded Loop** — the entire daily cycle end-to-end, hermetically in dry-run, with all day-1 invariants present.
3. **L2 — Reliability Spine & Proof-of-Run** — scheduled, self-healing, self-proving (depends on L1 close).
4. **L3 — Operations Surface** — the authenticated staff dashboard (status board ∥ L2; trust/value panels after L2).
5. **L4 — Hardening & Go-Live Readiness** — retention, balance alerts, breaker calibration, failure-injection, go-live scaffolding, security gate (depends on L1+L2+L3).

> **NO bead advances the go-live ladder** (`shadow → seed → canary → full`). The ladder is a post-L4, human-authorized RUNTIME event (research §6.6 / ADR-024). No build requirement flips a mode to `full`.

## Live-clinic guarantee (AGENTS.md RULE 3)

The clinic is already operating with real patients booked months ahead. Every build layer is hermetic by default: no real SMS and no real ClinicCards write are enabled by building software. Every bead touching a real-capable chokepoint (`smsSender`, guarded write-back) ships the fail-closed mode flag + allowlist AT the chokepoint in the SAME bead (mode-flag⊗chokepoint⊗allowlist atomic unit).

## Coverage summary

- Spec build requirements: 45 (FR/NFR across L1–L4) + 7 deferred/non-goal (DEF-*) → 100% mapped to ≥1 bead.
- TDD test IDs: full Static/Unit/Data/Contract/Integration/E2E/Release catalog → 100% assigned (release/runtime gates named for traceability; REL-SEED-DELIV-01 is a runtime rung, NOT a build bead).

## Success Criteria

- `br ready` exposes only the current layer gate, starting with Data 0001 and then progressing through Data → L1 → L2/L3 → L4 as dependencies close.
- Every build spec requirement and TDD test ID is named by at least one implementing task bead.
- All real-capable side effects remain behind fail-closed chokepoints with allowlists; no bead flips `SEND_MODE` or `CRM_WRITE_MODE` to `full` or performs a real send/write.
- The completed graph is build-shippable and go-live-ready only after L4; the `shadow → seed → canary → full` ladder remains a separate human-authorized runtime process.

# Data Layer 0001 — Core schema, indexes, DB-enforced invariants, clock seam, reaper/purge bodies

## SOURCE OF TRUTH WARNING

This bead is a quick-reference derived from:
- **Spec**: `docs/spec/2026-06-28-dentino-system-spec.md` — §5 FR-L1-DATA-01, NFR-L1-DATA-03 (DB-enforced parts), NFR-L2-DATA-04 (function bodies) (PRIMARY)

- **Research (cite, don't copy SQL except the named objects)**: §5.3 schema contract, §5.5 state, §5.7 concurrency SQL, ADR-008/012/014/016/019.

You MUST read research §5.3 and §5.7 directly for the exact DDL. This bead names the required objects; the research file is authoritative for column shapes.

## Coordination Protocol (MANDATORY — read before writing code)

Coordinated through Agent-Mail + file reservations + br state. Use the project wrappers — do not call `br update`/`br close` directly:
```bash
bin/br-claim <bead-id>     # reserves files, sends [<bead-id>] Start mail, sets in_progress
bin/br-complete <bead-id>  # after committed+pushed+tests pass: sends Complete mail, closes bead, syncs .beads/, releases reservations
```
Wrapper invocation must produce Agent-Mail [<bead-id>] Start and [<bead-id>] Complete audit messages through `bin/br-claim` / `bin/br-complete`; raw `br update --status` or `br close` is not an acceptable substitute.
If a wrapper errors, fix the cause (server down, file conflict, missing env). Do not bypass.

## Context

The root of the build. Every `reminder_messages` projection and every later layer depends on this schema existing first.

## Spec Requirements (verbatim)

### FR-L1-DATA-01 — Base Table Inventory (spec §5)
> The v1 schema shall create the full base-table inventory up front in the `app` schema.

**Acceptance Criteria**
- AC-FR-L1-DATA-01-a: The following 13 base tables exist in `app`: `patients`, `reminder_runs`, `reminder_days`, `reminder_messages`, `message_templates`, `cliniccards_status_policy`, `consent_events`, `cancellation_circuits`, `crm_visit_write_locks`, `inbound_events`, `crm_fetch_log`, `crm_visit_facts`, and `audit_log`.
- AC-FR-L1-DATA-01-b: Base tables, indexes, checks, triggers, and generated database types match the research §5.3 schema contract without hand-editing generated types.
- AC-FR-L1-DATA-01-c: Later v1 layers do not relax L1 base-table invariants or change base-table columns except through explicitly scoped additive views, functions, cron schedules, or data migrations allowed by the strategy.
- AC-FR-L1-DATA-01-d: Forward-compatibility fields needed for v1.2 channels, including `reminder_messages.channel` and `message_templates.buttons`, are present but do not activate app-channel scope in v1.

### NFR-L1-DATA-03 — Day-1 Invariants I1, I3, I4, and Fenced Side Effects (DB-enforced parts) (spec §5)
> The core row-state and side-effect invariants shall be active from L1 and never deferred.

**Acceptance Criteria owned here (the DB objects; behavioral enforcement lives in run-reminders/confirm/write-back beads):**
- AC-NFR-L1-DATA-03-a: I1 single-use is DB-enforced by the `action_locked_at is null` CAS, the `one_action_requires_lock` CHECK, and the `reminder_messages_action_lock_guard` trigger; one successful Confirm/Cancel action consumes the action lock and a second action cannot record a second business outcome.
- (Supports AC-NFR-L1-DATA-03-b/c/d/e: the `appointment_fingerprint` column, `claimed_or_live_token_required` CHECK, and the columns the supersede/fenced/atomic behavior bind to ship here.)

### NFR-L2-DATA-04 — I2 function bodies present day-1 (scheduled later in L2/L4) (spec §5)
- The `maintenance.reap_stale_sends()` and `maintenance.purge_privacy()` **bodies** are present from `0001`/`0002` per strategy §4.1; the `pg_cron` *schedules* are L2/L4. (This bead provides the body for `reap_stale_sends()`; the schedule is L2.)

### Forward-compat & DB clock (research §5.3/§5.7, ADR-023)
- Frozen forward-compat fields (present, unused in v1): `reminder_messages.channel` default `'sms'`; `message_templates.buttons jsonb`; `message_templates (key,channel,language)` shape; v1 `message_kind` CHECK (`initial_reminder`/`catchup_reminder`/`reschedule_notice`/`time_change_notice`).
- `app.now()` clock wrapper: returns `clock_timestamp()` in prod; under `APP_ENV=test` reads the `app.test_now` GUC when set. The DB mirror of `_shared/clock.ts`.
- The two partial-unique idempotency indexes + `message_templates_one_active`.

## Tests To Pass (verbatim from TDD)

### PGTAP-SCHEMA-01 — Tier 2 / Rung B / Owner L1
> The 13 `app` base tables, schemas, checks, indexes, triggers, forward-readiness fields, and required RPC/view/function names exist.

### DRIFT-SCHEMA-01 — Tier 7 / Rung B / Owner L1-L4
> After any migration/object change, `supabase gen types typescript --local` regenerates `database.types.ts`; any unexpected diff fails the gate; the generated file is not hand-edited.

## Files to Create/Modify
- `supabase/migrations/0001_core_schema.sql` — all 13 base tables, runtime indexes, the two partial-unique idempotency indexes, `one_action_requires_lock` CHECK, `claimed_or_live_token_required` CHECK, `reminder_messages_action_lock_guard` trigger, `message_templates_one_active`, `app.now()`, `appointment_fingerprint`, forward-compat fields, `maintenance.reap_stale_sends()` body.
- `supabase/functions/_shared/database.types.ts` — regenerated via `supabase gen types typescript --local` (never hand-edited).
- `tests/pgtap/schema.sql` — PGTAP-SCHEMA-01.

## Acceptance Criteria (this bead is done when)
1. All AC-FR-L1-DATA-01-a..d hold; `PGTAP-SCHEMA-01` green.
2. AC-NFR-L1-DATA-03-a DB objects exist (CAS column, CHECK, trigger).
3. `app.now()` + `app.test_now` seam works; reaper/purge body present.
4. `DRIFT-SCHEMA-01`: regenerate types, `git diff --exit-code` clean. Schema↔types no-drift is non-skippable.

## Gotchas & Anti-Patterns
- Do NOT "add the table now, the trigger later" — I1's CAS + CHECK + trigger all ship in `0001` (strategy §5.1 day-1 set).
- Do NOT hand-edit `database.types.ts` to satisfy TypeScript (AC-NFR-L1-TEST-02-c).
- Forward-compat fields are present but inert — do NOT wire app-channel logic in v1.

## Dependencies
- **Blocked by:** none (root of the build).
- **Blocks:** `0002` security core; therefore all of L1.
- **Layer:** data-layer (root). **Labels:** `l1`, `data-layer`.

### NFR-L1-DATA-02 — Schema Separation, RLS, Roles, and RPC Boundary (CORE — spec §5)
> The data layer shall expose only role-scoped, RPC/view-mediated access to Edge Functions and staff surfaces.

**Acceptance Criteria (the L1 core; L3 adds staff admin RPCs/views, optional DLR role added in L2):**
- AC-NFR-L1-DATA-02-a: Schemas `app`, `api`, `private`, and `maintenance` exist with `app` base tables not exposed directly through public APIs.
- AC-NFR-L1-DATA-02-b: RLS is enabled and forced on every `app` table, default-deny is the baseline, and base-table grants are absent for public and staff callers unless explicitly specified by research §6.3.2.
- AC-NFR-L1-DATA-02-c: Core DB roles exist: `dentino_confirm_api`, `dentino_confirm_definer`, `dentino_run_api`, `dentino_maintenance_runner`, and `dentino_maintenance_definer`.
- AC-NFR-L1-DATA-02-e: The public confirm function uses `dentino_confirm_api` and never receives `service_role`.
- AC-NFR-L1-DATA-02-f: Public RPCs exist with the exact API names `api.lookup_reminder_by_token`, `api.prepare_reminder_action`, `api.record_reminder_action`, and `api.finish_reminder_action`.
- AC-NFR-L1-DATA-02-i: Definer functions use the research-defined security hygiene, including fixed search paths, token-only lookups where applicable, fail-closed timeouts, and no caller-supplied dynamic SQL.

> Deferred to their layers (NOT this bead): AC-NFR-L1-DATA-02-d (conditional DLR role → L2 if built), AC-NFR-L1-DATA-02-g (L3 staff admin RPCs `update_message_template`/`resolve_held_cancels`/`reenable_sms_reminders`), AC-NFR-L1-DATA-02-h (`api.record_sms_status` → L2 if DLR built).

### PGTAP-GRANT-01 — Tier 2 / Rung B / Owner L1/L3
> `anon`, `dentino_confirm_api`, and `authenticated` have no prohibited base-table access; `dentino_confirm_api` executes only the four public RPCs; staff views expose no token, nonce, claim, or full-phone secrets.

(L1 core asserts the public/anon/`dentino_confirm_api` grants + the four-RPC restriction; the staff-view extension is L3.)

### PGTAP-RLS-01 — Tier 2 / Rung B / Owner L1-L4
> RLS is enabled and forced on every `app` table; Data API exposure is limited to `api` views/RPCs.

### PGTAP-DEFINER-01 — Tier 2 / Rung B / Owner L1-L4
> Every `SECURITY DEFINER` function uses `search_path = ''`, a non-login non-superuser owner, revoked `PUBLIC` execute, no caller-supplied dynamic SQL, and fail-closed role timeouts where required.

## Files to Create/Modify
- `supabase/migrations/0002_rls_policies.sql` — `app`/`api`/`private`/`maintenance` schemas; default-deny; RLS enable+FORCE on every `app` table; the research §6.3.2 per-role base-table grant matrix; core roles (`dentino_confirm_api`/`_definer`, `dentino_run_api`, `dentino_maintenance_runner`/`_definer`); the four `api` RPCs; `private.token_digest`; `maintenance.purge_privacy()` body.
- `tests/pgtap/grants.sql`, `tests/pgtap/rls.sql`, `tests/pgtap/definer.sql`.
- Regenerate `supabase/functions/_shared/database.types.ts` (DRIFT-SCHEMA-01).

## Acceptance Criteria (this bead is done when)
1. AC-NFR-L1-DATA-02-a/b/c/e/f/i hold; `PGTAP-GRANT-01` (core), `PGTAP-RLS-01`, `PGTAP-DEFINER-01` green.
2. No base-table grant to `anon`/`authenticated`/`dentino_confirm_api`; `dentino_confirm_api` executes only the four public RPCs.
3. `service_role` is never used by the confirm path.
4. Schema↔types no-drift re-asserted (DRIFT-SCHEMA-01).

- NEVER reintroduce `service_role` for the confirm fn (research §4.2 Tension 1 — the fourth RPC `finish_reminder_action` exists precisely so a no-table-grant caller can record the write-back outcome).
- The four RPC signatures are a FROZEN interface (strategy §4.2) — later layers bind to them, never break them.

- **Blocks:** all of L1.
- **Layer:** data-layer (root). **Labels:** `l1`, `data-layer`, `live-clinic` (privilege boundary).

# EPIC: L1 — Hermetic Guarded Loop

## SOURCE OF TRUTH WARNING

- **Spec**: `docs/spec/2026-06-28-dentino-system-spec.md` — §3, §4, §5, §6, §7 L1-owned FR/NFR + §8 NFR-L1-SAFE-01/02, NFR-L1-COMP-01/02, NFR-L1-TEST-01/02

- **Research (cite)**: §5.2, §5.3, §5.5, §5.6, §5.7, §5.8, §6.3, §6.5

## Coordination Protocol (MANDATORY)

Any implementation work under this bead uses the project wrappers:
```bash

bin/br-complete <bead-id>   # only after committed+pushed+tests pass
```

## Overview

Completes the entire daily reminder cycle for one `target_date`, end-to-end, hermetically in dry-run, **with all day-1 invariants present** (strategy §5.1). XL because the loop and its guards are inseparable. L1 is where the two real-capable chokepoints (`smsSender`, guarded write-back) first exist — so the fail-closed modes + allowlists + the hermetic harness are enforced from the first line of each.

## Internal build order (strategy §6 — parallelize only inside a gate)

- **Gate 1 — Foundation** (blocks all of L1): `_shared/http.ts` chokepoint + hermetic harness + APP_ENV boot guard; `clock.ts`/`app.now()` + `tokens.ts`/`phone.ts` digest seams.
- **Gate 2 — Parallel build** (depends on Gate 1): clinicCardsClient + cassettes ∥ templates/sender render ∥ confirm-page chrome ∥ smsSender (SEND_MODE+allowlist) ∥ guarded write-back (CRM_WRITE_MODE+allowlist) ∥ scope sentinels.

- **Gate 4 — L1 close** (depends on Gate 3): the L1 DoD gate. Closing this unlocks L2 + the L3 status-board sub-part.

## Success Criteria

- L1 foundation, parallel, convergence, and close beads complete in the stated gate order; L2 and L3 status-board remain blocked until L1 close.
- The hermetic no-egress harness, APP_ENV guard, `smsSender` SEND_MODE+allowlist, and guarded write-back CRM_WRITE_MODE+allowlist all exist at their chokepoints from first implementation.
- Token minting, send claiming, and SMS render remain one run-reminders bead; GET-safe confirm, interstitial, nonce POST, CAS, CRM re-fetch/fingerprint, and breaker remain one confirm bead.
- L1 DoD gates are green: no real egress, pgTAP core, confirm E2E, reconciliation-shortfall subset, and schema/types no-drift.

- **Blocks:** L2, L3 status-board.

## Context
The single outbound-HTTP chokepoint and the hermetic test harness. This is the mechanical embodiment of RULE 3: "no test touches a real patient" becomes load-bearing from the first HTTP client. Blocks everything in L1 that fetches/sends/writes.

## Spec Requirements (verbatim)

### FR-L1-PLAT-03 (http.ts portion) — Shared Library Inventory (spec §3)
- AC-FR-L1-PLAT-03-a: `_shared/http.ts` is the only outbound HTTP chokepoint for CRM, SMS, heartbeat, and optional provider-webhook verification clients.
- AC-FR-L1-PLAT-03-f: New outbound network code in any layer routes through `_shared/http.ts`; direct `fetch` outside the chokepoint fails the quality gate.

### NFR-L1-SAFE-01 — Hermetic No-Egress Harness (spec §8)
> No dev, test, or CI run may send a real SMS or write to the real ClinicCards CRM.
- AC-NFR-L1-SAFE-01-a: All outbound HTTP is routed through `_shared/http.ts`.

# L1-C2 — `confirm/index.ts` (GET-safe⊗nonce-POST⊗single-use-CAS⊗Cancel-interstitial⊗breaker ATOMIC) + footer opt-out

## SOURCE OF TRUTH WARNING
- **Spec**: `docs/spec/2026-06-28-dentino-system-spec.md` — FR-L1-WEB-01, FR-L1-WEB-02, FR-L1-WEB-03 (L1 mechanism), FR-L1-WEB-04, NFR-L1-WEB-08, NFR-L1-DATA-03 (I1 CAS behavioral), NFR-L1-COMP-01-b (consent_events append-only) (PRIMARY)
- **TDD**: `docs/tdd/2026-06-28-dentino-system-tdd.md` — UT-ACTIONS-01, E2E-AUTOFETCH-01..08, E2E-NONCE-01..08, E2E-TOKEN-01, E2E-DOUBLEPOST-01, PGTAP-CONCURRENCY-03, E2E-OPT-OUT-01, E2E-NOJS-01 (PRIMARY) (breaker velocity tests E2E-BREAKER-* are L4-owned calibration)
- **Strategy**: `docs/strategy/2026-06-27-dentino-layer-strategy.md` — §3.1, §5.1 #3 (full capability-flow Cancel day-1), §6 gate 3 (keep the full Cancel flow in ONE bead)
- **Research (cite)**: §5.4, §5.5, §5.7c (CAS predicate), §6.3, ADR-010, ADR-014, ADR-015, ADR-019, ADR-020, ADR-022.

## Coordination Protocol (MANDATORY)
```bash
bin/br-claim <bead-id>
bin/br-complete <bead-id>   # only after committed+pushed+tests pass
```

Wrapper invocation must produce Agent-Mail `[<bead-id>] Start` and `[<bead-id>] Complete` audit messages through `bin/br-claim` / `bin/br-complete`; raw `br update --status` or `br close` is not an acceptable substitute.

## ATOMIC UNIT (strategy §6 gate 3 / §5.1 #3 — do not split)
Keep side-effect-free `GET`/`HEAD`⊗nonce-backed `POST /prepare`⊗single-use CAS `POST /action`⊗Cancel interstitial⊗expiry⊗re-fetch+fingerprint guard⊗the velocity breaker-that-halts-writes in THIS bead. The first time Cancel exists, the ENTIRE unit exists. Auto-fetch immunity is binary.

## Context
The public confirm/cancel page and capability flow. Uses `dentino_confirm_api` + the four `api` RPCs (never `service_role`). Invokes the guarded write-back (L1-B5) for Confirm/Cancel.

## Spec Requirements (verbatim)

### FR-L1-WEB-01 — Public Confirm Endpoints (spec §7)
- AC-FR-L1-WEB-01-a: `GET /r/{token}` renders the appointment confirmation page and performs zero business writes.
- AC-FR-L1-WEB-01-b: `HEAD /r/{token}`, link previews, crawlers, query parameters, and method overrides perform zero business writes.
- AC-FR-L1-WEB-01-c: `POST /r/{token}/prepare` creates the nonce-backed action preparation required by the capability flow.
- AC-FR-L1-WEB-01-d: `POST /r/{token}/action` is the only endpoint that records Confirm, Cancel, or page opt-out state changes.
- AC-FR-L1-WEB-01-e: Missing, expired, not-found, superseded, or stale-CRM tokens fail without leaking whether a real patient or visit exists.
- AC-FR-L1-WEB-01-f: Token-page responses include the no-store, no-referrer, noindex/noarchive controls from research §5.4/§6.3 so raw tokens are not leaked through caches, referrers, robots, or monitoring.
- AC-FR-L1-WEB-01-g: `/action` rejects missing, expired, replayed, cross-action, or tampered nonces; cross-site signals; disallowed content types; query-string actions; and method overrides, with zero DB business writes and zero CRM calls.

### FR-L1-WEB-02 — Confirm Action Flow (spec §7)
- AC-FR-L1-WEB-02-a: Confirm is a one-tap patient action after page render and requires a valid action nonce.
- AC-FR-L1-WEB-02-b: Confirm consumes the single-use action lock through the research §5.7c CAS predicate, including action lock empty, actionable send state, unexpired token, not superseded, and live appointment still in the future.
- AC-FR-L1-WEB-02-c: Confirm revalidates the live ClinicCards visit and policy before write-back.
- AC-FR-L1-WEB-02-d: Double POST records exactly one business action and leaves the second attempt as an idempotent already-used response.
- AC-FR-L1-WEB-02-e: Successful Confirm updates dashboard state and write-back outcome within the research-defined minutes-scale expectation.
- AC-FR-L1-WEB-02-f: Confirm and Cancel action POSTs re-check the actionable-row predicate inside the CAS, including `status in ('sent','delivered','send_unknown')`, unexpired token, not superseded, and live appointment still in the future.

### FR-L1-WEB-03 (L1 mechanism portion) — Full Cancel Capability Flow and Mass-Cancel Breaker (spec §7)
- AC-FR-L1-WEB-03-a: Cancel cannot be completed from `GET`; it requires an interstitial, nonce-backed POST, single-use action lock, expiry check, live re-fetch, and fingerprint guard.
- AC-FR-L1-WEB-03-b: The interstitial foregrounds rescheduling by phone before the destructive cancel confirmation.
- AC-FR-L1-WEB-03-c: The destructive action label is explicit Ukrainian copy equivalent to cancelling without rescheduling.
- AC-FR-L1-WEB-03-d: The breaker counts only valid nonce-backed cancel intents represented by the research predicate: recorded Cancel response with the single-use action lock consumed.
- AC-FR-L1-WEB-03-e: Velocity hard-open halts CRM writes and moves affected cancels to `pending_staff_review` at >=4 valid cancels in any rolling 10-minute window or >=6 valid cancels in any rolling 30-minute window for the target date.
- AC-FR-L1-WEB-03-f: Daily amber warns while continuing at >=ceil(0.4 * sent) cancels for the target date.
- AC-FR-L1-WEB-03-g: Daily hard-ceiling requires staff acknowledgement before further auto-writes at >max(8, ceil(0.6 * sent)) cancels for the target date.
- (AC-FR-L1-WEB-03-h staff resolution → L3; AC-FR-L1-WEB-03-i calibration → L4.)

### FR-L1-WEB-04 — Footer Opt-Out Flow (spec §7)
- AC-FR-L1-WEB-04-a: Footer opt-out requires nonce-backed POST and updates `sms_reminders_enabled=false` plus an append-only `consent_events` row.
- AC-FR-L1-WEB-04-b: Opt-out does not record Confirm/Cancel and does not consume the appointment action lock.
- AC-FR-L1-WEB-04-d: The opt-out design follows the contract/healthcare-management lawful-basis framing in ADR-015.
- (AC-FR-L1-WEB-04-c staff re-enable RPC → L3.)

### NFR-L1-COMP-01 (consent-events portion) — Consent, Lawful Basis, and PII Minimization (spec §8)
- AC-NFR-L1-COMP-01-b: `consent_events` records opt-out and staff re-enable history append-only.

### NFR-L1-WEB-08 — Works Without JavaScript (spec §7)
- AC-NFR-L1-WEB-08-a: The server renders HTML forms for every state-changing action.
- AC-NFR-L1-WEB-08-b: Forms use hidden nonce fields generated by the prepare/action contract.
- AC-NFR-L1-WEB-08-c: Playwright JS-disabled tests cover Confirm, Cancel interstitial, destructive Cancel, stale/expired token, and opt-out paths.
- AC-NFR-L1-WEB-08-d: JavaScript enhancements, if ever added, cannot be required for the secure path.

### NFR-L1-DATA-03 (I1 CAS behavioral portion) (spec §5)
- AC-NFR-L1-DATA-03-a (behavioral): one successful Confirm/Cancel action consumes the action lock and a second action cannot record a second business outcome.

## Tests To Pass (verbatim from TDD)

### UT-ACTIONS-01 — Tier 1 / Rung A / Owner L1
> Action predicates classify Confirm, Cancel, opt-out, expired, superseded, stale, and terminal states exactly as the CAS/RPC contract expects.

### E2E-AUTOFETCH-01, E2E-AUTOFETCH-02, E2E-AUTOFETCH-03, E2E-AUTOFETCH-04, E2E-AUTOFETCH-05, E2E-AUTOFETCH-06, E2E-AUTOFETCH-07, E2E-AUTOFETCH-08 — Tier 5 / Rung C / Owner L1
> E2E-AUTOFETCH-01: `GET /r/{token}` changes 0 business rows, 0 consent rows, 0 breaker counts, 0 CRM calls, and consumes no nonce.
> E2E-AUTOFETCH-02: `HEAD /r/{token}` has the same zero-write result.
> E2E-AUTOFETCH-03: `OPTIONS` and unsupported safe-method probes have the same zero-write result.
> E2E-AUTOFETCH-04: 30x-followed redirect/preload fetch of the token page has the same zero-write result.
> E2E-AUTOFETCH-05: Image/script/link preview preload of `/r/{token}` has the same zero-write result and no third-party request.
> E2E-AUTOFETCH-06: `?action=confirm|cancel|unsubscribe` query parameters do not act.
> E2E-AUTOFETCH-07: `_method=POST` or other method override tricks do not act.
> E2E-AUTOFETCH-08: Auto-submitting/crawled form vectors do not record action, opt-out, CRM write, or breaker count.

### E2E-NONCE-01, E2E-NONCE-02, E2E-NONCE-03, E2E-NONCE-04, E2E-NONCE-05, E2E-NONCE-06, E2E-NONCE-07, E2E-NONCE-08 — Tier 5 / Rung C / Owner L1
> E2E-NONCE-01: Missing nonce POST fails with zero DB business writes and zero CRM calls.
> E2E-NONCE-02: Replayed nonce fails and does not consume a second action.
> E2E-NONCE-03: Cross-action nonce fails, for example confirm nonce submitted as cancel.
> E2E-NONCE-04: Expired nonce fails.
> E2E-NONCE-05: Nonce for a superseded row fails.
> E2E-NONCE-06: Cross-site Origin/Sec-Fetch-Site signals fail closed.
> E2E-NONCE-07: Wrong or empty content type fails closed.
> E2E-NONCE-08: Tampered render fingerprint in signed nonce fails closed.

### E2E-TOKEN-01 — Tier 5 / Rung C / Owner L1
> Malformed, valid-shape unknown, expired, superseded, stale-CRM, and terminal-status tokens render identical neutral invalid/expired responses with no oracle.

### E2E-DOUBLEPOST-01 — Tier 5 / Rung C / Owner L1
> Two concurrent valid action POSTs record exactly one business action, exactly one action lock, and <=1 CRM write; second renders already-recorded state.

### PGTAP-CONCURRENCY-03 — Tier 2 / Rung B / Owner L1
> Double action CAS yields exactly one `action_locked_at`; second action affects 0 rows; trigger rejects unlock/re-respond.

### E2E-OPT-OUT-01 — Tier 5 / Rung C / Owner L1/L3
> Footer opt-out requires nonce-backed POST, appends `consent_events`, sets SMS preference false, does not consume appointment action, and GET cannot opt out.

### E2E-NOJS-01 — Tier 5 / Rung C / Owner L1
> JavaScript-disabled Playwright completes Confirm, Cancel interstitial, destructive Cancel, stale/expired token, and opt-out flows using server-rendered forms.

## Files to Create/Modify
- `supabase/functions/confirm/index.ts` (GET/HEAD/prepare/action; nonce contract; single-use CAS; full Cancel interstitial + breaker; footer opt-out; no-store/no-referrer/noindex headers) — shares the file with the chrome bead (L1-B3).
- `tests/integration/confirm-page.test.ts`, `tests/unit/actions.test.ts`, `tests/pgtap/concurrency.sql` (CAS case).

## Acceptance Criteria (this bead is done when)
1. All cited ACs hold; the full E2E-AUTOFETCH/NONCE/TOKEN/DOUBLEPOST/OPT-OUT/NOJS + UT-ACTIONS-01 + PGTAP-CONCURRENCY-03 green.
2. Auto-fetch immunity is binary: GET/HEAD/preview/query/override → zero business writes, zero CRM calls.
3. Cancel cannot complete from GET; the velocity breaker halts writes (moves to `pending_staff_review`).
4. Double POST → exactly one business action.

## Gotchas & Anti-Patterns
- NEVER a "GET-cancel for now" (strategy §3.1.13 forbidden) — the full Cancel unit ships here.
- Token error responses must be a single neutral page with no oracle leaking whether a patient/visit exists.

## Dependencies
- **Blocked by:** L1-B3 (confirm chrome), L1-B5 (write-back). (Uses the four `api` RPCs + tokens from foundation.)
- **Blocks:** L1 close.
- **Layer:** L1 (gate 3). **Labels:** `l1`, `web`, `live-clinic`.

# L1-F2 — Determinism seams: `clock.ts`/`app.now()` · `tokens.ts` · `phone.ts`

## SOURCE OF TRUTH WARNING
- **Spec**: `docs/spec/2026-06-28-dentino-system-spec.md` — FR-L1-PLAT-03 (clock.ts/tokens.ts/phone.ts), FR-L1-RUN-01 (Kyiv math seam), FR-L1-RUN-03 (token shape), FR-L1-CRM-03-d / NFR-L1-COMP-01-c (phone HMAC) (PRIMARY)
- **TDD**: `docs/tdd/2026-06-28-dentino-system-tdd.md` — UT-KYIV-01, UT-TOKEN-01, UT-PHONE-01 + bootstrap "Determinism Seams" table (PRIMARY)
- **Strategy**: `docs/strategy/2026-06-27-dentino-layer-strategy.md` — §5.1 #8 (Kyiv date math + seams), §6 gate 1 (ordering only)
- **Research (cite)**: §4.4, §5.7, §6.5, ADR-016, ADR-023.

## Coordination Protocol (MANDATORY)
```bash
bin/br-claim <bead-id>
bin/br-complete <bead-id>   # only after committed+pushed+tests pass
```

Wrapper invocation must produce Agent-Mail `[<bead-id>] Start` and `[<bead-id>] Complete` audit messages through `bin/br-claim` / `bin/br-complete`; raw `br update --status` or `br close` is not an acceptable substitute.

## Context
The pure-function deterministic primitives every time/token/timezone/phone-sensitive test depends on. Foundation gate — blocks the L1 build beads.

## Spec Requirements (verbatim)

### FR-L1-PLAT-03 (seam portion) — Shared Library Inventory (spec §3)
- AC-FR-L1-PLAT-03-b: `_shared/clock.ts` owns Kyiv/date math and deterministic test-time injection.
- AC-FR-L1-PLAT-03-c: `_shared/tokens.ts` owns 128-bit token generation, nonce generation, HMAC digesting, and seeded test RNG injection.
- AC-FR-L1-PLAT-03-e (phone.ts portion): `_shared/phone.ts` exists with responsibilities matching the research file map (E.164 normalization, never returns full phone for persistence).

### FR-L1-RUN-01 (clock seam portion) — Kyiv Target-Date Computation (spec §6)
- AC-FR-L1-RUN-01-a: `target_date` is never derived from UTC date alone.
- AC-FR-L1-RUN-01-d: Kyiv DST and local-date fixtures are part of the deterministic test suite.

### FR-L1-RUN-03 (token shape portion) — Token Minting (spec §6)
- AC-FR-L1-RUN-03-b: Tokens are 128-bit CSPRNG values encoded as 22-character base64url and stored only as HMAC digests.

### Phone PII minimization (spec §4/§8)
- AC-FR-L1-CRM-03-d: Full phone numbers are never persisted; only `phone_hmac`, `phone_last4`, and non-identifying phone metadata may be stored.
- AC-NFR-L1-COMP-01-c: Full phone numbers are not stored in Dentino tables, logs, cassettes, heartbeat payloads, or inbound events.

## Tests To Pass (verbatim from TDD)

### UT-KYIV-01 — Tier 1 / Rung A / Owner L1
> Fixed winter, summer, spring-forward, fall-back, near-midnight, and noon-window UTC instants produce the expected Europe/Kyiv `run_date_kyiv` and `target_date_kyiv`; target date is never derived from UTC alone.

### UT-TOKEN-01 — Tier 1 / Rung A / Owner L1
> Seeded RNG emits deterministic 128-bit, 22-character base64url tokens and nonces; production path uses CSPRNG; stored value is HMAC digest only.

### UT-PHONE-01 — Tier 1 / Rung A / Owner L1
> Phone normalization accepts valid Ukrainian mobile inputs, rejects missing/invalid values, produces E.164, and never returns full phone values for persistence.

(Bootstrap seam contract, verbatim: the RNG seam uses a seeded 16-byte stream in tests and asserts the exact 22-character base64url capability token shape; tests must never shorten tokens for convenience. The Kyiv fixture matrix includes winter EET, summer EEST, spring-forward, fall-back, near-midnight Kyiv where UTC is still the prior date, and every noon-window UTC slot `09:00`, `09:30`, `10:00`, `10:30`.)

## Files to Create/Modify
- `supabase/functions/_shared/clock.ts` (Edge clock; prod = real, test = `app.test_now` GUC mirror — pairs with `app.now()` from `0001`).
- `supabase/functions/_shared/tokens.ts` (injected RNG default `crypto.getRandomValues`; HMAC digest; signed action nonce; never shortens token).
- `supabase/functions/_shared/phone.ts` (E.164 `380…` normalization; HMAC + last4 only).
- `tests/unit/{tokens,phone}.test.ts`, `tests/harness/{clock,rng,kyiv-fixtures}.ts`, `tests/unit/smoke.test.ts` (Rung A).

## Acceptance Criteria (this bead is done when)
1. AC-FR-L1-PLAT-03-b/c/e (phone), FR-L1-RUN-01-a/d, FR-L1-RUN-03-b, FR-L1-CRM-03-d, AC-NFR-L1-COMP-01-c hold.
2. `UT-KYIV-01`, `UT-TOKEN-01`, `UT-PHONE-01` green; no test shortens a token; a UTC-derived target date fails.

## Gotchas & Anti-Patterns
- The RNG/clock seams must be read-only and inert in prod (GUC unset/ignored unless `APP_ENV=test`) — they must NOT alter prod entropy or the one-winner proofs.
- `phone.ts` must never return a full phone for persistence — only HMAC + last4.

## Dependencies
- **Blocked by:** Data layer (`0001` provides `app.now()` that `clock.ts` mirrors).
- **Blocks:** L1 gate-2 build beads + run-reminders.
- **Layer:** L1 (foundation gate). **Labels:** `l1`, `foundation`.

# L1-B1 — `_shared/clinicCardsClient.ts` + ClinicCards cassettes (REST read, chunk-split, fail-closed)

## SOURCE OF TRUTH WARNING
- **Spec**: `docs/spec/2026-06-28-dentino-system-spec.md` — FR-L1-CRM-01, FR-L1-CONF-01 (ClinicCards confirmations), NFR-L1-COMP-01-d (redact-at-write) (PRIMARY)

- **Research (cite)**: §4.1, §5.2, §5.6, §10, ADR-001, ADR-011.

## Coordination Protocol (MANDATORY)

```bash
bin/br-claim <bead-id>
bin/br-complete <bead-id>   # only after committed+pushed+tests pass
```

Wrapper invocation must produce Agent-Mail `[<bead-id>] Start` and `[<bead-id>] Complete` audit messages through `bin/br-claim` / `bin/br-complete`; raw `br update --status` or `br close` is not an acceptable substitute.

## Context
The CRM integration path — read tomorrow's visits + patients via the ClinicCards REST API (NOT browser automation). Routes through `_shared/http.ts`.

## Spec Requirements (verbatim)

### FR-L1-CRM-01 — ClinicCards REST Read Integration (spec §4)
> The system shall read tomorrow's ClinicCards visits and associated patients through the ClinicCards REST API, not browser automation.
- AC-FR-L1-CRM-01-a: The CRM client supports `GET /visits?from=&to=` and patient lookup through `GET /patients/{ids}` or the vendor-confirmed equivalent.
- AC-FR-L1-CRM-01-b: The client chunks/splits patient requests when URL length or provider limits require it and fails closed on truncated or ambiguous lists.
- AC-FR-L1-CRM-01-c: The engine records fetch provenance in `crm_fetch_log` with redaction-at-write and typed facts in `crm_visit_facts`.
- AC-FR-L1-CRM-01-d: ClinicCards token casing, filters, pagination, status semantics, timestamp precision, and visit-by-id availability are build-time confirmations owned by L1.

### FR-L1-CONF-01 (ClinicCards portion) — Build-Time External Confirmations (spec §8)
- AC-FR-L1-CONF-01-a: ClinicCards token header casing, visit filters, patient pagination, status meanings, timestamp precision, optimistic concurrency support, cancel semantics, and visit reuse behavior are confirmed before relying on them.
- AC-FR-L1-CONF-01-b: Cross-day move detection is resolved by L1; absent visit-by-id support, v1 kills the old token and flags staff.

### NFR-L1-COMP-01-d (redact-at-write portion) (spec §8)
- AC-NFR-L1-COMP-01-d: Raw ClinicCards payload logs are redacted at write time and purged by L4 retention jobs.

## Tests To Pass (verbatim from TDD)

### CONTRACT-CRM-01 — Tier 3 / Rung C / Owner L1
> ClinicCards `GET /visits` and `GET /patients` cassettes parse the documented envelope, field shapes, timestamp formats, pagination/chunking, and status semantics.

### CONTRACT-CRM-02 — Tier 3 / Rung C / Owner L1
> Patient lookup chunks split on 414/400, dedupe IDs, cap rate, and fail closed on truncation or ambiguous partial lists.

### CONTRACT-CRM-03 — Tier 3 / Rung C / Owner L1/L4
> Build-time ClinicCards confirmations are captured as contract assertions or owner release-gate evidence: token casing, filters, patient pagination, visit-by-id, timestamp precision, optimistic concurrency, cancel semantics, and visit reuse.

(Bootstrap cassette groups, verbatim: ClinicCards visits — `GET /visits` normal, empty, malformed/truncated, changed/moved, terminal, 429/500. ClinicCards patients — `GET /patients` normal, missing patient, merged/unresolved, invalid phone, chunk split 414/400.)

## Files to Create/Modify
- `supabase/functions/_shared/clinicCardsClient.ts` (`GET /visits`, `GET /patients`; routes via http.ts; writes `crm_fetch_log` redacted + `crm_visit_facts`).
- `tests/fixtures/cassettes/` ClinicCards visit + patient cassettes (sanitized).
- `tests/integration/` contract-test wiring for CONTRACT-CRM-01/02/03.

## Acceptance Criteria (this bead is done when)
1. AC-FR-L1-CRM-01-a..d, FR-L1-CONF-01-a/b, NFR-L1-COMP-01-d hold.
2. `CONTRACT-CRM-01/02/03` green; chunk-split fails closed on truncation/ambiguity.
3. Phones stay in-memory only; `crm_fetch_log` is redacted-at-write.

## Gotchas & Anti-Patterns
- Fail CLOSED on a truncated or ambiguous patient list — never proceed on a partial list.
- Cross-day-move build-gate (research §10): absent visit-by-id lookup, kill the old token + flag staff; never auto-send a cross-day notice.

## Dependencies
- **Blocked by:** L1 foundation (http.ts chokepoint, seams).
- **Blocks:** run-reminders convergence.
- **Layer:** L1 (gate 2). **Labels:** `l1`, `crm`.

- **Research (cite)**: §4.2 (canonical template seed — copy lives ONLY in §4.2 + the DB `message_templates` seed), §6.5 suite B, ADR-005/009/010.

## Coordination Protocol (MANDATORY)
```bash
bin/br-claim <bead-id>
bin/br-complete <bead-id>   # only after committed+pushed+tests pass
```

Wrapper invocation must produce Agent-Mail `[<bead-id>] Start` and `[<bead-id>] Complete` audit messages through `bin/br-claim` / `bin/br-complete`; raw `br update --status` or `br close` is not an acceptable substitute.

## Context
Renders Ukrainian SMS reminders from editable DB templates while enforcing the two-segment budget. The canonical default copy lives in research §4.2 + the `message_templates` seed — cite it, do not duplicate it here.

## Spec Requirements (verbatim)

### FR-L1-RUN-04 — SMS Rendering, Sender, and Segment Budget (spec §6)
> The system shall render Ukrainian SMS reminders from editable templates while enforcing the two-segment budget.
- AC-FR-L1-RUN-04-a: The default v1 sender ID is `Dentino`.
- AC-FR-L1-RUN-04-b: The template contract supports `{{name}}`, `{{date}}`, `{{time}}`, `{{confirm_url}}`, `{{clinic_phone}}`, and the multi-language/channel-ready fields defined by `message_templates`.
- AC-FR-L1-RUN-04-c: The production default reminder copy matches the research §4.2 template seed and uses the no-spaces clinic phone `+380679876111`.
- AC-FR-L1-RUN-04-d: Rendered reminders must fit within two UCS-2 SMS segments, with a hard budget of 134 UCS-2 characters for the configured default and fallback.
- AC-FR-L1-RUN-04-e: Long rendered names trigger the name-overflow fallback that drops the name while preserving the clinic phone and confirm link.
- AC-FR-L1-RUN-04-f: The renderer never shortens the token URL and never transliterates Ukrainian text to save segments.
- AC-FR-L1-RUN-04-g: SMS golden tests cover Cyrillic text, link integrity, segment math, and placeholder failures.

### FR-L1-PLAT-03 (templates.ts/sender.ts portion) (spec §3)
- AC-FR-L1-PLAT-03-d: `_shared/sender.ts` defines the channel-agnostic `send()` interface.
- AC-FR-L1-PLAT-03-e (templates.ts portion): `_shared/templates.ts` exists with responsibilities matching the research file map.

### NFR-L1-COMP-02 — Logistics-Only Message Content (spec §8)
- AC-NFR-L1-COMP-02-a: SMS and confirm-page appointment copy may include name/display snapshot, date, time, clinic identity, confirm URL, and clinic phone.
- AC-NFR-L1-COMP-02-b: SMS and confirm-page copy do not include diagnosis, procedure, treatment plan, clinical notes, payment request, banking details, passwords, or SMS-code requests.
- AC-NFR-L1-COMP-02-c: Template validation and review reject clinical or payment-content additions before activation.

## Tests To Pass (verbatim from TDD)

### UT-TEMPLATE-01 — Tier 1 / Rung A / Owner L1/L3
> Default and fallback templates require the approved placeholders, sender ID `Dentino`, no-spaces clinic phone, and no unresolved placeholders; the production default body is 130 UCS-2 chars/two segments, and the fallback remains within the same hard budget.

### PROP-SEGMENT-01 — Tier 1 / Rung A / Owner L1
> Property test generates adversarial Cyrillic, Latin, emoji, RTL, zero-width, empty, and 200-character names; every render is <=2 segments and <=134 UCS-2 chars, or uses the no-name fallback.

### SMS-LINK-01 — Tier 5 / Rung C / Owner L1
> Rendered SMS contains exactly one full `https://r.dentino.com.ua/r/<token>` URL, token is 22-char base64url, not empty, not truncated, not duplicated, and no literal placeholder survives.

### SMS-CYRILLIC-01 — Tier 5 / Rung C / Owner L1
> Golden default and name-overflow bodies byte-compare for Cyrillic correctness and include the no-spaces clinic phone.

### SMS-KYIV-01 — Tier 5 / Rung C / Owner L1
> SMS `date` and `time` render from Europe/Kyiv visit time; UTC substitution fails the test.

### SMS-GOLDEN-01 — Tier 5 / Rung C / Owner L1/L3
> `tests/fixtures/sms-golden` corpus covers representative fixtures, long-name fallback, placeholder failures, and deliberate review-visible updates.

### STATIC-CONTENT-01 — Tier 0 / Rung A / Owner L1
> SMS and confirm-page templates remain logistics-only and reject clinical, payment, banking, password, or SMS-code content.

## Files to Create/Modify
- `supabase/functions/_shared/templates.ts` (render placeholders; 2-segment budget; name-overflow fallback; never shorten URL / never transliterate).
- `supabase/functions/_shared/sender.ts` (the `send()` interface — frozen seam for v1.2 channels).
- `tests/unit/templates.test.ts`, `tests/fixtures/sms-golden/`.

## Acceptance Criteria (this bead is done when)
1. AC-FR-L1-RUN-04-a..g, FR-L1-PLAT-03-d/e, NFR-L1-COMP-02-a..c hold.
2. `UT-TEMPLATE-01`, `PROP-SEGMENT-01`, `SMS-LINK-01`, `SMS-CYRILLIC-01`, `SMS-KYIV-01`, `SMS-GOLDEN-01`, `STATIC-CONTENT-01` green.

## Gotchas & Anti-Patterns
- NEVER shorten the token URL or transliterate Ukrainian to save a segment (AC-FR-L1-RUN-04-f) — it reads as low-trust bulk SMS.
- The canonical copy lives only in research §4.2 + the DB seed — do not fork a third copy into code comments.

# L1-B3 — Confirm-page chrome (design tokens, inline brand, a11y, trust copy)

## SOURCE OF TRUTH WARNING
- **Spec**: `docs/spec/2026-06-28-dentino-system-spec.md` — NFR-L1-WEB-05, NFR-L1-WEB-06, NFR-L1-WEB-07, NFR-L1-WEB-09, NFR-L1-WEB-10, NFR-L1-WEB-11, FR-L1-WEB-12 (PRIMARY) (NFR-L1-WEB-08 no-JS flows live in the confirm behavior bead)
- **TDD**: `docs/tdd/2026-06-28-dentino-system-tdd.md` — E2E-A11Y-CONFIRM-01 (PRIMARY)
- **Strategy**: `docs/strategy/2026-06-27-dentino-layer-strategy.md` — §3.1, §5.8 (the seven hard confirm-page constraints), §6 gate 2 (ordering only)
- **Research (cite)**: §5.8, §6.2, §6.3, ADR-022; `docs/design/mockups/confirm-page.html` is the build reference + §6.5 Playwright seed.

## Coordination Protocol (MANDATORY)
```bash
bin/br-claim <bead-id>
bin/br-complete <bead-id>   # only after committed+pushed+tests pass
```

Wrapper invocation must produce Agent-Mail `[<bead-id>] Start` and `[<bead-id>] Complete` audit messages through `bin/br-claim` / `bin/br-complete`; raw `br update --status` or `br close` is not an acceptable substitute.

## Context
The static patient-facing confirm-page surface: brand/trust + accessibility, built from the design tokens. The reference is `docs/design/mockups/confirm-page.html`. (Behavioral flows — GET/prepare/action/Cancel/opt-out — are the separate confirm/index.ts bead.)

## Spec Requirements (verbatim)

### NFR-L1-WEB-05 — Zero Third-Party Assets (spec §7)
- AC-NFR-L1-WEB-05-a: Rendered confirm-page HTML references no external fonts, scripts, trackers, analytics, CDNs, pixels, or remote images.
- AC-NFR-L1-WEB-05-b: Any brand mark or design token used on the page is inline or served from the same app-owned origin; the Dentino vector logo source follows the research §5.8 inline black/white asset rule.
- AC-NFR-L1-WEB-05-c: Automated page tests fail if third-party network requests occur.

### NFR-L1-WEB-06 — Cyrillic-Complete System Fonts (spec §7)
- AC-NFR-L1-WEB-06-a: CSS uses a Cyrillic-complete system font stack, not webfont downloads.
- AC-NFR-L1-WEB-06-b: Ukrainian appointment, trust, and action copy renders without missing glyphs in browser tests.
- AC-NFR-L1-WEB-06-c: The visual design remains usable if custom brand fonts are unavailable.

### NFR-L1-WEB-07 — Confirm Page Size Budget (spec §7)
- AC-NFR-L1-WEB-07-a: The full patient-facing confirm-page response is <=50 KB gzipped.
- AC-NFR-L1-WEB-07-b: The size test includes inline CSS, inline brand asset, trust copy, forms, and state-specific closure pages.
- AC-NFR-L1-WEB-07-c: Adding optional dashboard or marketing assets to the public page fails review.

### NFR-L1-WEB-09 — Confirm Page Contrast (spec §7)
- AC-NFR-L1-WEB-09-a: Text and controls meet at least WCAG-AA contrast and the researched measured minimum of 6.46:1 for muted text.
- AC-NFR-L1-WEB-09-b: Colors that fail AA for text are decorative only.
- AC-NFR-L1-WEB-09-c: Automated accessibility tests fail on contrast regressions.

### NFR-L1-WEB-10 — Confirm Page Tap Targets (spec §7)
- AC-NFR-L1-WEB-10-a: Primary actions, destructive actions, phone links, and footer action controls have tap targets of at least 48 px.
- AC-NFR-L1-WEB-10-b: Focus states are visible for keyboard and switch-control users.
- AC-NFR-L1-WEB-10-c: Mobile viewport tests fail if controls overlap, shrink below target size, or require precision tapping.

### NFR-L1-WEB-11 — Ukrainian, Zoom, and Information Hierarchy (spec §7)
- AC-NFR-L1-WEB-11-a: The document uses `lang="uk"`.
- AC-NFR-L1-WEB-11-b: Body text is at least 18 px and appointment date/time is the largest visual fact on the page.
- AC-NFR-L1-WEB-11-c: The page remains usable at 200% zoom and does not disable user scaling.
- AC-NFR-L1-WEB-11-d: The page does not rely on modal-only, countdown-only, or hover-only interactions.
- AC-NFR-L1-WEB-11-e: The information hierarchy is clinic identity, appointment fact, actions, why-you-received-this, and telephone fallback.

### FR-L1-WEB-12 — Confirm Page Trust Copy (spec §7)
- AC-FR-L1-WEB-12-a: The page includes Ukrainian "why you received this" copy equivalent to receiving the message because the patient has a planned visit at Dentino, Lviv.
- AC-FR-L1-WEB-12-b: The page includes Ukrainian anti-scam copy stating the clinic does not ask for payment, bank details, passwords, or SMS codes.
- AC-FR-L1-WEB-12-c: The clinic phone is available as a `tel:` link on the page and especially around Cancel/reschedule states.
- AC-FR-L1-WEB-12-d: Engagement KPIs are based on recorded nonce-backed actions, not scanner-contaminated GET views.

## Tests To Pass (verbatim from TDD)

### E2E-A11Y-CONFIRM-01 — Tier 5 / Rung C / Owner L1
> Confirm page has zero third-party assets, system Cyrillic fonts, <=50 KB gzipped response, AA contrast, >=48 px tap targets, visible focus, `lang="uk"`, 200% zoom usability, and correct trust copy.

## Files to Create/Modify
- `supabase/functions/confirm/index.ts` (the page-chrome render portion; HTML/inline CSS/inline brand asset) — coordinate with the confirm behavior bead which owns GET/prepare/action.
- inline CSS generated from `docs/design/design-tokens.json`; inline black/white Dentino logo (research §5.8).
- Playwright a11y test seeded from `docs/design/mockups/confirm-page.html`.

## Acceptance Criteria (this bead is done when)
1. AC-NFR-L1-WEB-05/06/07/09/10/11 + FR-L1-WEB-12 all hold.
2. `E2E-A11Y-CONFIRM-01` green (zero third-party requests; <=50 KB gzipped; AA contrast incl. 6.46:1 muted; >=48 px targets; `lang="uk"`; 200% zoom; trust + anti-scam copy present).

## Gotchas & Anti-Patterns
- Zero third-party assets is binary — the a11y test fails on ANY external network request.
- Engagement KPIs use recorded nonce-backed actions, never GET page views (scanner-contaminated).

## Dependencies
- **Blocked by:** L1 foundation.
- **Blocks:** confirm/index.ts behavior convergence (shares the file).
- **Layer:** L1 (gate 2). **Labels:** `l1`, `web`.

## Coordination Protocol (MANDATORY)
```bash

bin/br-complete <bead-id>   # only after committed+pushed+tests pass
```

## RULE 3 — mode-flag⊗chokepoint⊗allowlist ATOMIC UNIT (do not split)
This bead ships the `SEND_MODE` check + `SEND_ALLOWLIST` enforcement IN the same bead as the provider-send chokepoint. There is NO "send first, add the guard later" bead. The `SEND_MODE` check happens in `smsSender` immediately before the provider call. The real provider-request code is built and cassette-tested here but is made reachable only by a human-authorized `SEND_MODE` flip at go-live — this bead never flips a mode.

## Context
The channel-agnostic SMS send chokepoint. At runtime it is the STUB (records would-send intent; `SEND_MODE='off'`). The real TurboSMS/AlphaSMS request code is built + cassette-tested here. Routes through `_shared/http.ts`.

## Spec Requirements (verbatim)

### FR-L1-RUN-05 — SMS Provider Integration and Ambiguous Sends (spec §6)
> The SMS provider client shall support TurboSMS as the v1 primary route with AlphaSMS fallback readiness, while treating ambiguous provider outcomes safely.

# L1-B5 — Guarded ClinicCards write-back + CRM_WRITE_MODE + CRM_WRITE_ALLOWLIST + write-lease + run-owned reaper [LIVE-CLINIC]

## SOURCE OF TRUTH WARNING
- **Spec**: `docs/spec/2026-06-28-dentino-system-spec.md` — FR-L1-CRM-05, NFR-L1-SAFE-02 (CRM_WRITE_MODE + CRM_WRITE_ALLOWLIST portion), NFR-L1-DATA-03 (fenced-write portion) (PRIMARY)

- **Strategy**: `docs/strategy/2026-06-27-dentino-layer-strategy.md` — §3.1, §5.1 #2/#10 (fail-closed modes + fenced side effects day-1), §6 gate 2 (ordering only)
- **Research (cite)**: §4.1, §5.2, §5.6, §5.7 (the canonical write-lock/fenced SQL), ADR-007, ADR-014, ADR-020, ADR-024.

## Coordination Protocol (MANDATORY)
```bash
bin/br-claim <bead-id>
bin/br-complete <bead-id>   # only after committed+pushed+tests pass
```

Wrapper invocation must produce Agent-Mail `[<bead-id>] Start` and `[<bead-id>] Complete` audit messages through `bin/br-claim` / `bin/br-complete`; raw `br update --status` or `br close` is not an acceptable substitute.

## RULE 3 — mode-flag⊗chokepoint⊗allowlist ATOMIC UNIT (do not split)
This bead ships the `CRM_WRITE_MODE` check + `CRM_WRITE_ALLOWLIST` enforcement IN the same bead as the guarded write-back chokepoint. The `CRM_WRITE_MODE` check happens immediately before `PUT` or any fallback destructive CRM call. No "write first, add the guard later" bead. This bead never flips a mode.

## Context
The single guarded write-back chokepoint: re-fetch → fingerprint compare → status-policy check → fenced `PUT /visits` → post-write re-fetch. Invoked by the confirm/cancel action path and by run-reminders. Routes through `_shared/http.ts`.

## Spec Requirements (verbatim)

### FR-L1-CRM-05 — Guarded Confirm/Cancel Write-Back (spec §4)
- AC-FR-L1-CRM-05-a: Confirm writes `CONFIRMED` only when the current ClinicCards status policy allows it.
- AC-FR-L1-CRM-05-b: Cancel writes `CANCELLED` by default only after the full Cancel capability flow completes and the breaker permits the write.
- AC-FR-L1-CRM-05-c: Write-back re-fetches the live visit immediately before writing, compares the render/action fingerprint, writes all required ClinicCards fields through the vendor-supported `PUT /visits` shape, and re-fetches after the write to verify the landed status.
- AC-FR-L1-CRM-05-d: The write path uses `crm_visit_write_locks` and fenced owner-token updates; a stale actor affects zero rows and makes zero ClinicCards write calls.
- AC-FR-L1-CRM-05-e: `crm_visit_write_locks` is an approximately 90-second per-visit lease around live re-fetch, ClinicCards write, and post-write re-fetch; a live lease makes another Dentino-originated action wait/no-op, and a stale lease is stealable under the research §5.7d rule.
- AC-FR-L1-CRM-05-f: The write path never holds a DB transaction or advisory transaction lock across ClinicCards HTTP.
- AC-FR-L1-CRM-05-g: `DELETE /visits`, if supported, is staff-approved fallback only and never the default automated cancel path.
- AC-FR-L1-CRM-05-h: Write-back failures are retried at most twice under the idempotent re-fetch rules, then surfaced as red needs-attention items with immediate staff escalation.
- AC-FR-L1-CRM-05-i: A patient action committed before a CRM write is re-driven by the fenced write-back reaper until it lands or becomes an explicit `error`; it is not left as a human-only-exit crash gap.

### NFR-L1-SAFE-02 (CRM_WRITE_MODE + CRM_WRITE_ALLOWLIST portion) — Fail-Closed Modes (spec §8)
- AC-NFR-L1-SAFE-02-d: `CRM_WRITE_MODE` is checked in the guarded write-back immediately before `PUT` or any fallback destructive CRM call.
- AC-NFR-L1-SAFE-02-f: In any non-`full` write mode, `CRM_WRITE_ALLOWLIST` permits only owner-created designated test visit IDs; empty/unset allowlist refuses all writes.
- AC-NFR-L1-SAFE-02-h: Only `full` lifts the allowlist guard.

### NFR-L1-DATA-03 (fenced-write portion) — Fenced Side Effects (spec §5)
- AC-NFR-L1-DATA-03-d: Every protected write is fenced by owner token and expected state; if ownership is lost or a fenced update affects zero rows, no further external side effect is made.

## Tests To Pass (verbatim from TDD)

### IT-WRITEBACK-01 — Tier 4 / Rung C / Owner L1
> Guarded Confirm/Cancel write-back re-fetches, compares fingerprint, honors status policy, dispatches at most two idempotent retries, post-write re-fetches, and surfaces hard failures.

### IT-WRITEBACK-REAPER-01 — Tier 4 / Rung C / Owner L1
> Action committed before CRM write is re-driven by the run-owned reaper before reconcile until landed or explicit error; stale actor makes zero external calls.

### PGTAP-CONCURRENCY-04 — Tier 2 / Rung B / Owner L1
> Two per-visit write-lock contenders yield exactly one live lease; stale owner affects 0 rows and cannot release the stealer lease.

### E2E-TOCTOU-01 — Tier 5 / Rung C / Owner L1
> Live re-fetch returns changed/moved/terminal/reassigned facts; guarded write-back refuses, writes nothing, flags, and re-renders current facts.

### E2E-WRITELEASE-01 — Tier 5 / Rung C / Owner L1
> Two write-backs to one visit serialize through `crm_visit_write_locks`; loser waits/no-ops; stale owner makes zero external calls.

### IT-MODES-01 (write portion) — Tier 4 / Rung C / Owner L1
> ... `CRM_WRITE_MODE` absent, empty, or malformed default to refuse side effects; non-full empty allowlists refuse all writes ... (this bead proves the write-side chokepoint refusal).

## Files to Create/Modify
- the guarded write-back module (research §5.2 "CRM write-back" row) — invoked by `confirm/index.ts` and `run-reminders`; `CRM_WRITE_MODE` check immediately before `PUT`; `CRM_WRITE_ALLOWLIST` enforcement; `crm_visit_write_locks` ~90 s lease; fenced owner-token updates; run-owned reaper (`crm_writeback_ok is not true` predicate).
- `tests/integration/write-back.test.ts`, `tests/pgtap/concurrency.sql` (write-lock case).

## Acceptance Criteria (this bead is done when)
1. AC-FR-L1-CRM-05-a..i, NFR-L1-SAFE-02-d/f/h, NFR-L1-DATA-03-d hold.
2. `IT-WRITEBACK-01`, `IT-WRITEBACK-REAPER-01`, `PGTAP-CONCURRENCY-04`, `E2E-TOCTOU-01`, `E2E-WRITELEASE-01`, write-side `IT-MODES-01` green.
3. Stale actor affects 0 rows and makes 0 ClinicCards write calls; no DB/advisory tx lock held across HTTP.

## Gotchas & Anti-Patterns
- `PUT CANCELLED` is the default (preserves history); `DELETE` is staff-approved fallback only — never the default automated cancel.
- Never hold a DB transaction across the ClinicCards HTTP call (AC-FR-L1-CRM-05-f).
- This bead does NOT flip `CRM_WRITE_MODE` (RULE 3).

- **Blocked by:** L1 foundation; CRM client (L1-B1).
- **Blocks:** run-reminders + confirm convergence.
- **Layer:** L1 (gate 2). **Labels:** `l1`, `crm`, `live-clinic`.

## Context
Sentinel tests that prove the deferred/non-goal set stays OUT of v1 while preserving schema/interface readiness. These guards prevent silent scope creep — a deferred feature accidentally built is as much a defect as a missing one.

## Spec Requirements (verbatim — the deferral commitments these sentinels enforce)

### DEF-v1.1-NUDGE-01 — No-Reply Nudge (Target: v1.1) (spec §9)
- AC-DEF-v1.1-NUDGE-01-a: v1 does not send a second no-reply SMS.
- AC-DEF-v1.1-NUDGE-01-b: v1.1 adds `message_kind='no_reply_nudge'` and its own partial unique key on `(visit_id, target_date)` for that kind.
- AC-DEF-v1.1-NUDGE-01-c: A nudge is eligible only after a delivered initial reminder with no recorded response and after fresh pre-send revalidation.
- AC-DEF-v1.1-NUDGE-01-d: v1.1 mints a fresh token, expires the prior token, and preserves exactly one live link/action capability.
- AC-DEF-v1.1-NUDGE-01-e: Raw token storage is never introduced to support nudge re-sending.

### DEF-v1.1-PROVIDER-01 — Provider DLR/Idempotency/Retry (Target: v1.1) (spec §9)
- AC-DEF-v1.1-PROVIDER-01-a: v1 correctness does not depend on DLR callbacks; sent-based reconciliation and patient actions remain authoritative.
- AC-DEF-v1.1-PROVIDER-01-b: If DLR callbacks are built, they use `sms-status/index.ts`, `dentino_sms_webhook_api`, and `api.record_sms_status`.
- AC-DEF-v1.1-PROVIDER-01-c: Provider idempotency mode is not upgraded beyond the safe baseline until written provider guarantees justify it.
- AC-DEF-v1.1-PROVIDER-01-d: Provider retry tooling never blind-retries ambiguous sends; unresolved ambiguity remains `send_unknown` unless strict dedupe is proven.

### DEF-v1.2-CHANNEL-01 — Viber/WhatsApp/Telegram (Target: v1.2) (spec §9)
- AC-DEF-v1.2-CHANNEL-01-a: v1 sends SMS only and stores no per-patient channel discovery state.
- AC-DEF-v1.2-CHANNEL-01-b: Future Viber/WhatsApp/Telegram senders plug in behind the `send()` interface.
- AC-DEF-v1.2-CHANNEL-01-c: `reminder_messages.channel`, `message_templates.channel`, and `message_templates.buttons jsonb` remain available as additive readiness fields.
- AC-DEF-v1.2-CHANNEL-01-d: Future app-channel callbacks feed the same response/action service and cannot bypass single-use locks, live CRM revalidation, status policy, write-back mode guards, or the mass-cancel breaker.
- AC-DEF-v1.2-CHANNEL-01-e: App-native Cancel requires an equivalent destructive second step or `pending_staff_review` handoff.

### DEF-v1.2-PRODUCT-02 — Multi-Language/Lead-Time/Doctor-Template/Analytics (Target: v1.2) (spec §9)
- AC-DEF-v1.2-PRODUCT-02-a: v1 stores template language/channel shape for future use but does not implement automatic patient-language selection.
- AC-DEF-v1.2-PRODUCT-02-b: v1 uses the configured next-day lead time; configurable per-segment/per-doctor lead-time rules are v1.2.
- AC-DEF-v1.2-PRODUCT-02-c: v1 does not require per-doctor templates, while the template versioning model can be extended without changing the core action spine.
- AC-DEF-v1.2-PRODUCT-02-d: v1 dashboard value/action metrics do not imply a full analytics product; broader confirm/cancel/no-reply analytics are v1.2 extensions.

### DEF-vNext-SCHED-01 — Two-Way Scheduling (Target: vNext) (spec §9)
- AC-DEF-vNext-SCHED-01-a: v1 does not implement conversational slot search, booking by text, or automated appointment rescheduling.
- AC-DEF-vNext-SCHED-01-b: v1 Cancel offers rescheduling by phone and staff workflow, not automated two-way scheduling.
- AC-DEF-vNext-SCHED-01-c: Future scheduling must preserve the channel-agnostic action spine and guarded CRM write-back model.

### DEF-NONGOAL-MULTITENANT-01 — Multi-Tenant (Explicit non-goal) (spec §9)
- AC-DEF-NONGOAL-MULTITENANT-01-a: v1 targets a single confirmed clinic and does not add `clinic_id` to every base table.
- AC-DEF-NONGOAL-MULTITENANT-01-b: Configuration remains non-hardcoded where practical, but no multi-clinic UI, routing, billing, or tenant isolation is built.
- AC-DEF-NONGOAL-MULTITENANT-01-c: A future multi-tenant migration, if ever needed, is treated as a bounded new product decision rather than hidden v1 scope.

### DEF-NONGOAL-TELEMED-01 — Telemedicine/Clinical Workflow (Explicit non-goal) (spec §9)
- AC-DEF-NONGOAL-TELEMED-01-a: v1 does not implement telemedicine visits, diagnosis collection, treatment advice, clinical intake, or clinical document exchange.
- AC-DEF-NONGOAL-TELEMED-01-b: Reminder flows remain appointment-logistics workflows and do not become clinical communication workflows.

### SCOPE-NONGOAL-01 — Tier 0 / Rung A / Owner L1-L4
> v1 code has no conversational booking, auto-rescheduling, telemedicine, diagnosis intake, clinical-document exchange, or multi-tenant routing surface.

### SCOPE-DEF-NUDGE-01 — Tier 1 / Rung A / Owner v1.1 sentinel
> v1 has no second no-reply SMS send path; any future no-reply nudge must require a fresh token and one live capability.

### SCOPE-DEF-CHANNEL-01 — Tier 1 / Rung A / Owner v1.2 sentinel
> v1 sends SMS only; future channels remain behind `send()` and cannot bypass the action spine.

# L1-C1 — `run-reminders/index.ts` dry-run orchestration (token-mint⊗send-claim⊗render ATOMIC)

## SOURCE OF TRUTH WARNING
- **Spec**: `docs/spec/2026-06-28-dentino-system-spec.md` — FR-L1-RUN-01, FR-L1-RUN-02, FR-L1-RUN-03, FR-L1-CRM-02, FR-L1-CRM-03, FR-L1-CRM-04, NFR-L1-DATA-03 (token-mint atomic + I3/I4 behavioral) (PRIMARY)
- **TDD**: `docs/tdd/2026-06-28-dentino-system-tdd.md` — IT-RUN-01, IT-RUN-02, IT-IDEMPOTENCY-01, IT-TOKEN-CLAIM-01, IT-SUPERSEDE-01, IT-SUPERSEDE-PARTIAL-01, IT-RECON-01, PGTAP-CONCURRENCY-01, PGTAP-CONCURRENCY-02, UT-STATUS-01 (PRIMARY)
- **Strategy**: `docs/strategy/2026-06-27-dentino-layer-strategy.md` — §3.1, §5.1 #5/#6/#7 (I1/materialize/fingerprint day-1), §6 gate 3 (keep token-mint⊗send-claim⊗render in ONE bead)
- **Research (cite)**: §4.2, §5.2, §5.3, §5.5, §5.6, §5.7b (per-message claim SQL), ADR-008/010/012/013/014/020.

## Coordination Protocol (MANDATORY)
```bash
bin/br-claim <bead-id>
bin/br-complete <bead-id>   # only after committed+pushed+tests pass
```

Wrapper invocation must produce Agent-Mail `[<bead-id>] Start` and `[<bead-id>] Complete` audit messages through `bin/br-claim` / `bin/br-complete`; raw `br update --status` or `br close` is not an acceptable substitute.

## ATOMIC UNIT (strategy §6 gate 3 — do not split across beads)
Keep token-mint⊗send-claim⊗render in THIS bead. The claimer writes exactly one digest+expiry while the raw token stays in memory only for the SMS URL. Splitting this across beads would race or persist a raw token.

## Context
The reminder engine, dry-run orchestration (`SEND_MODE='off'`): compute Kyiv `target_date` → claim `reminder_days` lease → `GET /visits` → write `crm_visit_facts` → classify against `cliniccards_status_policy` (unknown → fail closed) → batch `GET /patients` (phones in-memory) → always-materialize one `reminder_messages` row per remindable visit (or policy-accounted skip) → pre-send revalidate → per-message claim (`pending→sending`, mint token in memory, commit digest+expiry+snapshot) → render SMS → stub send via `smsSender` → single-firing reconcile → run-owned write-back reaper.

## Spec Requirements (verbatim)

### FR-L1-RUN-01 — Kyiv Target-Date Computation (spec §6)
- AC-FR-L1-RUN-01-a: `target_date` is never derived from UTC date alone.
- AC-FR-L1-RUN-01-b: Each run records `utc_now`, `kyiv_now`, `run_date_kyiv`, and `target_date_kyiv`.
- AC-FR-L1-RUN-01-c: A mismatch between expected Kyiv target date and computed target date fails before sending or writing.

### FR-L1-RUN-02 — Always-Materialized Rows + Single-Firing Reconciliation (spec §6)
- AC-FR-L1-RUN-02-a: A run materializes a `reminder_messages` row for every currently observed remindable appointment or policy-accounted skip.
- AC-FR-L1-RUN-02-b: One ordinary reminder per `(visit_id, target_date)` is enforced for v1 initial/catch-up reminder kinds.
- AC-FR-L1-RUN-02-c: Single-firing reconciliation reports sent, skipped, failed, send_unknown, superseded, and unaccounted counts before a day can be considered complete.
- AC-FR-L1-RUN-02-d: Unaccounted current remindable appointments produce red health and prevent a success heartbeat.
- AC-FR-L1-RUN-02-e: Reconciliation accounts a current visit only with a non-superseded active row whose `appointment_fingerprint` matches the latest CRM fact; a stale sent row for moved facts does not account for the current appointment.
- AC-FR-L1-RUN-02-f: A visit that was previously remindable but vanishes from the latest fetch is red unless the system proves it became terminal, was Dentino-write-backed, or moved under the research §5.6/§10 cross-day rule.

### FR-L1-RUN-03 — Per-Message Claim, Token Minting, and Outcome Commit (spec §6)
- AC-FR-L1-RUN-03-a: The engine claims eligible `pending` rows using the research §5.7b per-message `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` one-winner claim before rendering and sending.
- AC-FR-L1-RUN-03-b: Tokens are 128-bit CSPRNG values encoded as 22-character base64url and stored only as HMAC digests.
- AC-FR-L1-RUN-03-c: Raw tokens exist only long enough to render the outbound link and are never logged or persisted.
- AC-FR-L1-RUN-03-d: Provider calls happen only after the row is committed to `sending` with its claim/token digest.
- AC-FR-L1-RUN-03-e: Send outcome commits are guarded by the message claim token; a stale worker cannot mark another worker's row.
- AC-FR-L1-RUN-03-f: A stale `sending` claim is reaped to `send_unknown` by the next firing, on-steal sweep, or L2 `pg_cron` backstop, and is not blindly resent.
- AC-FR-L1-RUN-03-g: A materialized sendable `pending` row has no live capability digest before claim; the claimer writes exactly one digest and expiry while the raw token remains only in memory for the SMS URL.

### FR-L1-CRM-02 — Data-Driven Remindability Policy (spec §4)
- AC-FR-L1-CRM-02-a: Statuses intended to be reminded, including `PLANNED` and `NOT_CONFIRMED`, are represented in `cliniccards_status_policy`.
- AC-FR-L1-CRM-02-b: Non-remindable, terminal, in-progress, tentative, moved, and unknown statuses are skipped or flagged according to policy.
- AC-FR-L1-CRM-02-c: A status missing from `cliniccards_status_policy` fails closed as `unknown_status`, creates staff attention, and never sends by default.
- AC-FR-L1-CRM-02-d: Policy changes are delivered by tracked data migrations, not by raw dashboard SQL or untracked hot edits.

### FR-L1-CRM-03 — Patient Eligibility and Skip Accounting (spec §4)
- AC-FR-L1-CRM-03-a: A sendable patient requires a valid mobile phone and enabled SMS reminder preference.
- AC-FR-L1-CRM-03-b: Missing phone, invalid phone, missing patient, unresolved/merged patient, changed `patient_id`, disabled SMS preference, unknown status, and non-remindable status each produce explicit skip reasons.
- AC-FR-L1-CRM-03-c: Skipped rows are materialized in `reminder_messages` when the appointment is observed so reconciliation can prove there are no silent omissions.
- (AC-FR-L1-CRM-03-d phone non-persistence enforced via `_shared/phone.ts`.)

### FR-L1-CRM-04 — Change Detection and Supersession (spec §4)
- AC-FR-L1-CRM-04-a: Each reminder row stores the current appointment fingerprint needed by the research-defined reconciliation and supersede rules.
- AC-FR-L1-CRM-04-b: A materially changed appointment may receive exactly one explicit change notice, while unchanged appointments never receive duplicate ordinary reminders.
- AC-FR-L1-CRM-04-c: Superseding a row expires the old token before any replacement capability can act.
- AC-FR-L1-CRM-04-d: If cross-day moves cannot be proven through ClinicCards, v1 kills the old token and flags staff instead of auto-sending a cross-day notice.

### NFR-L1-DATA-03 (atomic + I3/I4 behavioral portion) (spec §5)
- AC-NFR-L1-DATA-03-b: I3 supersede-kills-capability is enforced: a superseded row has its capability expired, `/action` cannot act on it, and late provider status cannot resurrect it.
- AC-NFR-L1-DATA-03-c: I4 action-implies-delivery is enforced: a valid Confirm/Cancel action on `send_unknown` promotes the row to `delivered` before write-back; footer opt-out is a separate preference path and does not satisfy I4.
- AC-NFR-L1-DATA-03-e: The token-mint, send-claim, and render unit is atomic in `run-reminders` and is not split across independent flows.

## Tests To Pass (verbatim from TDD)

### IT-RUN-01 — Tier 4 / Rung C / Owner L1
> One synthetic visit through `run-reminders` creates exactly one materialized row and one stub would-send intent with zero provider calls and zero CRM writes.

### IT-RUN-02 — Tier 4 / Rung C / Owner L1
> Every observed appointment is accounted for as sent, skipped, failed, send_unknown, superseded, pending, or unaccounted with explicit reason and no silent omission.

### IT-IDEMPOTENCY-01 — Tier 4 / Rung C / Owner L1/L2
> Double-fire, rerun, and catch-up do not duplicate ordinary reminders for `(visit_id,target_date)`; completed initial duplicate no-ops.

### IT-TOKEN-CLAIM-01 — Tier 4 / Rung C / Owner L1
> A materialized sendable `pending` row starts with no capability digest; the claim writes exactly one digest and expiry while raw token stays in memory only; crash before claim leaves a normal pending row, and crash after claim reaps to `send_unknown` without reconstructing or resending.

### IT-SUPERSEDE-01 — Tier 4 / Rung C / Owner L1
> Material change supersedes old row, expires old token, inserts exactly one replacement notice row, and old action POST returns neutral/0 rows.

### IT-SUPERSEDE-PARTIAL-01 — Tier 6 / Rung C / Owner L1
> Crash before supersede plus replacement insertion leaves current-fingerprint reconciliation red and retriable; crash after insertion but before replacement send leaves old token dead and the replacement unresolved as `pending`/`sending`/`send_unknown`.

### IT-RECON-01 — Tier 6 / Rung C / Owner L1
> Induced single-firing shortfall (`pending`, deleted materialized row, stale fingerprint, vanished unresolved) makes health red and unaccounted/pending count nonzero.

### PGTAP-CONCURRENCY-01 — Tier 2 / Rung B / Owner L1
> Two concurrent first `reminder_days` lease claims yield exactly one winner; a live `running` lease makes the loser return zero rows; no advisory transaction lock is held across HTTP.

### PGTAP-CONCURRENCY-02 — Tier 2 / Rung B / Owner L1
> Two per-message `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` claims never claim the same row; only retryable pre-submit failures re-enter `sending`.

### UT-STATUS-01 — Tier 1 / Rung A / Owner L1
> `cliniccards_status_policy` mapping treats remindable statuses as sendable and unknown/missing statuses as fail-closed `unknown_status`.

## Files to Create/Modify
- `supabase/functions/run-reminders/index.ts` (cron + manual entry; dry-run orchestration; the lease claim; classify; always-materialize; per-message claim atomic; stub send; single-firing reconcile; run-owned write-back reaper invocation).
- `tests/unit/{status-map,actions}.test.ts` (status mapping), `tests/integration/run-reminders.test.ts`, `tests/pgtap/concurrency.sql` (lease + per-message claim cases).

## Acceptance Criteria (this bead is done when)
1. All cited ACs hold; the listed tests are green.
2. The token-mint⊗send-claim⊗render unit is atomic; a stale `sending` claim reaps to `send_unknown` (never blind-resent).
3. Unknown status fails closed; unaccounted current remindable appointments are red.

## Gotchas & Anti-Patterns
- Never derive `target_date` from UTC alone; mismatch fails before sending (FR-L1-RUN-01).
- Never persist or log a raw token; only the HMAC digest persists.
- A superseded row's old token must be dead before any replacement can act (I3).

- **Blocked by:** L1-B1 (CRM client), L1-B2 (templates/sender), L1-B4 (smsSender), L1-B5 (write-back).
- **Blocks:** L1 close.
- **Layer:** L1 (gate 3). **Labels:** `l1`, `run`, `live-clinic`.

### FR-L2-RUN-06 — Scheduled Multi-Fire, Catch-Up, and Lease Steal (spec §6)
- AC-FR-L2-RUN-06-a: Noon execution is guarded by Europe/Kyiv local time, with the research-defined multi-fire UTC windows preventing DST/scheduler drift.
- AC-FR-L2-RUN-06-b: An automatic afternoon catch-up reclaims the target date and scans late bookings or changes without duplicating ordinary reminders.
- AC-FR-L2-RUN-06-c: `reminder_days` lease acquisition, heartbeat renewal, heartbeat-grace steal, and absolute TTL behavior follow the research §5.7a lease contract: heartbeat renewed about every 30 seconds, steal allowed after about 120 seconds without heartbeat, and the approximately 15-minute TTL remains only an absolute backstop.
- AC-FR-L2-RUN-06-d: Duplicate completed initial firings no-op unless the pass kind is catch-up/manual and explicitly allowed to rescan.
- AC-FR-L2-RUN-06-e: A crashed holder is reclaimable within approximately the heartbeat grace window and does not wait for the absolute TTL in normal recovery.

## Tests To Pass (verbatim from TDD)

### PGTAP-CONCURRENCY-05 — Tier 2 / Rung B / Owner L2
> With `app.test_now`, a live lease holder renewing heartbeat at <=30 seconds is never stolen; a stopped heartbeat is stealable after about 120 seconds; the 15-minute TTL is only the absolute backstop.

### IT-LEASE-STEAL-01 — Tier 6 / Rung C / Owner L2
> A dead holder is reclaimed after heartbeat grace; on-steal sweep immediately reaps orphaned `sending` rows; a live holder is not stolen.

### IT-IDEMPOTENCY-01 (catch-up portion) — Tier 4 / Rung C / Owner L1/L2
> Double-fire, rerun, and catch-up do not duplicate ordinary reminders for `(visit_id,target_date)`; completed initial duplicate no-ops.

# L2-2 — Reaper totality (pg_cron backstop) + multi-firing reconciliation + external dead-man's-switch + runtime budgets

## SOURCE OF TRUTH WARNING
- **Spec**: `docs/spec/2026-06-28-dentino-system-spec.md` — NFR-L2-DATA-04 (I2 totality), FR-L2-RUN-07 (reconciliation + proof-of-run), NFR-L2-RUN-08 (budgets) (PRIMARY)
